text:
maria: Heads-up — after merging Turnstile LoRA into cust/turnstile/v1 and shipping an int4 quantized variant (Q4f) to the canary pool, our invoice-search embedding eval shows a noticeable regression. Starting a quick triage thread.

sam: Can you paste the eval outputs and the exact model tag?

maria: Model: turnstile-lora-v1-q4f (merged -> quantized with bnb4 Q4f). Eval run command: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite invoice-embed --model turnstile-lora-v1-q4f --batch 128 --cache-prefix on
```
Quick metrics: MRR 0.12 (baseline int8: 0.18), recall@5 0.78 (baseline 0.92), avg_latency_per_query 38ms (baseline 48ms).

jin: Oof — that's a pretty big hit for embeddings. Any tokenizer or preprocessing differences in the merge?

maria: No tokenizer changes in the LoRA; merge was strictly the adapter weights. Quantization config: 
```
quant_backend: bnb
quant_mode: q4f
per_layer_scaling: true
```
We tried both with/without prefix cache — regression persists.

leo: Do you have an example query where embedding L2 jumped?

maria: Sample diff (cosine similarity):
`query: "Invoice #12948 payment due"`
- int8 baseline cos: 0.86 -> nearest invoice doc ID 413
- q4f cos: 0.59 -> nearest invoice doc ID 177
Small change but many queries swapped top hits.

qa_bot: Automated regression alert created: RG-2024-0923-01 (link: https://issues.redwood.ai/RG-2024-0923-01)

sam: My hunch — Q4f backend with per-layer scaling might be shifting the embedding subspace for adapter layers. Two quick experiments: 1) rerun with `quant_backend=nf4` 2) rerun disabling per-layer scaling. I'll kick them off.

sam: Running: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite invoice-embed --model turnstile-lora-v1-q4f --quant-backend nf4 --batch 128
```

ops-bot: Canary deployment created: canary/turnstile -> turnstile-lora-v1-q4f (pool: dedicated-canary-1)

sam: NF4 run finished: MRR 0.16, recall@5 0.86, latency ~40ms. Better but not fully back to int8.

jin: That's interesting — nf4 recovered most of the recall. Any idea which layer(s) contribute? We can run a layerwise ablation embedding to see which adapter layer quantization hurts most.

maria: Agreed. I'll run a quick layerwise pass with `rwi-eval --layer-scan`. Command: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite invoice-embed --model turnstile-lora-v1-q4f --quant-backend nf4 --layer-scan true --output /tmp/turnstile-layer-scan.json
```

leo: If NF4 helps, maybe we should change default quant backend for adapter-only quant in CUST pipelines. But let's confirm first. Also ping infra: does the canary route have any tokenization or preprocessing proxy differences?

ops-bot: infra note: dedicated-canary-1 uses same preprocess container as prod; no differences recorded this deploy.

maria: Layer-scan results (summary): adapter layer 3 and 4 show biggest drop when q4f is used vs nf4. Looks like low-rank adapter projections are sensitive to the bnb scale placement.

sam: Proposal: 1) rollback canary to int8 for customer traffic (safety) 2) patch quant pipeline to prefer nf4 for adapter-only LoRA quantization 3) open a follow-up to investigate bnb per-layer scale math.

maria: +1. I created a rollback PR: `rwi-deploy promote --model turnstile-lora-v1-int8 --route canary/turnstile --reason "embed regression"`

ops-bot: Deployment event: promoted turnstile-lora-v1-int8 -> canary/turnstile (change id: DPL-8791)

jin: I'll take the bnb scale investigation. Sam, can you parameterize a small grid (q4f + nf4, per-layer scaling true/false) and dump embedding distances so we can run clustering comparison?

sam: Yep. Grid queued. I'll post results in this thread when done.

maria: Thanks — next steps documented in RG-2024-0923-01. For immediate customer impact we've rolled back canary and alerted CS.

leo: Can CS message prepared? I'll draft a note: short explanation, mitigation (we rolled back), ETA for fix ~48-72h.

maria: Thanks all. If nf4 fixes on grid run, we can do a fast patch rollout and smoke test against the invoice-suite before customer traffic.

sam: Grid update (short): best config `quant_backend=nf4, per_layer_scaling=false` -> MRR 0.175, recall@5 0.91, latency 42ms. Looks close to baseline. I'll open a patch PR to change the adapter quantizer default and add unit tests for embedding drift.

maria: Perfect. Tagging the eval artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/evals/turnstile/1708427777-grid-scan.json

qa_bot: Regression ticket RG-2024-0923-01 status -> triaged (severity: high)

ops-bot: Reminder: schedule canary smoke test once PR merges.

maria: End of thread for now — thanks everyone.
